title: Verifier‑Assisted versus LLM‑Only Pre‑deployment Network‑Change Validation: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We measured whether integrating a deterministic pre‑deployment verifier (with at most one automated repair) increases the fraction of intent‑driven configuration proposals that pass semantic validation compared with accepting a single LLM candidate. In a preregistered paired design (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) we executed 300 paired intents (100 per difficulty stratum) using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic NetOps validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Each pair evaluated one shared_initial candidate under two conditions: baseline (accept single shot) and guarded (deterministic validation and ≤1 automated repair). Results: baseline 299/300 unflagged passes (0.9966667), guarded 300/300 (1.0); contingency n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; absolute paired difference = 0.0033333; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00,0.01] (bootstrap_seed = 1729, B = 10000). Under the supplied synthetic suite and repair budget the single‑shot generator was near ceiling, limiting observable marginal rescue by the guarded pipeline. All preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts are archived with the study id to support replication and follow‑ups that vary estimand conditioning, model strength, or repair budget.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to NetOps tasks such as intent→configuration translation, template synthesis, and automated repair. Operators require semantic guarantees—sequencing, reachability, and policy preservation—that syntactic checks alone cannot provide. Hybrid architectures pairing generative models with deterministic validators and bounded automated repair (generate→validate→repair) aim to reduce operational risk, but the measurable benefit depends on the evaluand (what is held fixed), the generator's single‑shot quality, validator expressiveness, and permitted repair budget.

We preregistered a paired experiment (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) to quantify the deterministic rescue achievable when the same single LLM candidate is evaluated under two treatments. For each intent the pipeline produced a single shared_initial candidate using the declared generator (gpt-5-mini) and compared: (a) baseline — accept the single candidate without repair, and (b) guarded — run a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) and allow at most one automated repair which itself is re‑validated. The core research question: does adding a deterministic verifier plus at most one automated repair increase the probability that a single LLM candidate passes semantic pre‑deployment validation compared with accepting that same single candidate without repair?

This paper reports a fully archived confirmatory run (300 paired intents stratified by difficulty). Contributions: (1) a preregistered paired evaluation isolating deterministic rescue under a shared_initial estimand that conditions on a single LLM draw per intent; (2) a complete execution and analysis bundle including validator traces and the single automated repair transcript archived with the run; (3) an artifact‑grounded interpretation of estimator conditioning, ceiling effects, and operational implications for NetOps pipelines. We explicitly note that the preregistered pilot (n = 60) intended for discordance estimation was not executed and no post‑preregistration power recalculation was performed, a decision that materially reduces inferential sensitivity when baseline performance is near ceiling.
sections.related_work:
Surveys and systems work document active efforts to apply LLMs to NetOps problems including intent translation, configuration synthesis, repair, and tool‑augmented orchestration [https://openalex.org/W4402742293; https://openalex.org/W4411015066; https://openalex.org/W4416927413]. Prior systems papers describe generate→validate→repair patterns and planner‑centric tool orchestration that call external validators to improve correctness; reported gains depend strongly on task formulation, validator coverage, and generation strategy [doi:10.1609/aaai.v40i40.40676; https://openalex.org/W4404240614]. Practitioner studies and surveys highlight operator skepticism about deployability despite high syntactic correctness in controlled experiments [https://openalex.org/W7167855398; https://openalex.org/W4416927413].

Two methodological gaps motivated our experiment. First, many prior comparisons conflate deterministic validator rescue with benefits from drawing additional independent model candidates (resampling); permitting resampling mixes generator variance effects with deterministic validator effects. Second, public NetOps benchmarks that emphasize semantic correctness (reachability, policy compliance) rather than syntactic validity are still limited in scope and adoption [https://openalex.org/W4415071524; https://openalex.org/W4392875514]. We address the first gap by conditioning on a single shared_initial candidate per intent, thereby isolating only the deterministic recovery achievable without additional independent model draws; this estimand is operationally relevant for policies that limit model calls per change request.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study preregistration (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) fixed the primary estimand: the absolute paired difference in the unflagged verifier‑pass proportion (guarded minus baseline) computed on paired cases that evaluate the same shared_initial candidate. Confirmatory design elements were frozen prior to main execution: planned analyzable pairs N = 300 (100 per difficulty stratum: low/medium/high), explicit inclusion/exclusion rules, the binary scoring rule (unflagged == pass), and the analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1). The optional pilot (n = 60) for discordance estimation was recorded in the preregistration but was not executed; no post‑preregistration recalculation of sample size was performed and this is declared in the Disclosure.

Task generation and synthetic suite. Tasks were produced deterministically by the registered task generator into a synthetic_topology_suite and stratified into difficulty bins using generator metadata (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, required_command_count). Representative intent patterns include shutdown_configure_restore (medium) and paired_link_atomic_mtu_change (hard). The task manifest records required_sequences and intent constraints for every item; the synthetic suite enforces protected_interface invariants and preserve_unspecified_state rules that the validator checks. Six representative tasks and their shared_initial responses are included among archived artifacts to illustrate typical difficulty and validator diagnostics.

Shared_initial protocol, model, and orchestration. The declared generator for shared_initial candidate production was gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json lists requested_model = "gpt-5-mini"). To implement the shared_initial estimand, the pipeline produced exactly one shared_initial generation per pair and reused that identical candidate for both baseline and guarded conditions. The guarded pipeline executed deterministic_netops_validator_v5 on the shared_initial candidate and, if flagged, invoked at most one automated repair attempt (repair budget ≤1). The repair routine is a constrained edit operator limited to localized sequencing or insertion edits and logs a repair provider trace. The baseline pipeline accepted the same shared_initial candidate unmodified. This design isolates deterministic validator/repair rescue from gains achievable by allowing independent resampling, verifier‑guided steering, or iterative generation.

Validator, scoring, and contamination controls. deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implements the preregistered full_intent_constraint_validation rule: deterministic checks for sequencing invariants (must_be_down_for_fields), required_command_count, preservation of unspecified state, reachability invariants encoded in the synthetic topology, and forbidden‑template protection (protected_interfaces). Scoring is binary (unflagged == pass); a candidate that remains flagged after the permitted repair attempts counts as a failure for the primary estimand. Contamination and negative controls were implemented per preregistration: one intentionally‑broken negative control per complexity stratum and automated invariant checks (pre/post reachability matrices). The run's contamination_summary.csv is empty, indicating no unexpected negative-control passes.

Execution contract and audit instrumentation. The confirmatory execution used adapter_family hosted_netops_gvr_v1 under execution_mode scientific_confirmatory. Execution manifest values (execution_manifest) reported: planned_episode_count = 600, completed_episode_count = 600, complete_pair_count = 300, model_calls_used = 301, maximum_model_calls = 600. Provider call auditing recorded hosted_model_call_event_count = 301, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 301, and stage_counts showing shared_initial_generation = 300 and repair = 1. Missingness rules were enforced: pairs with both calls failing due to outage would be excluded (none occurred); the run's missingness summary records zeros for failed or unscorable episodes.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and integrity. The hosted adapter completed the confirmatory run with completed_episode_count = 600 and complete_pair_count = 300; model_calls_used = 301 (300 shared_initial generations plus one repair call). Deterministic reconciliation confirms episode and provider‑call accounting and reports all_deterministic_consistency_checks_passed = true. The contamination summary is empty and missingness_summary.csv shows no excluded or failed episodes.

Marginal and paired outcome counts. Condition summary (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline successes = 299/300 (0.9966666666666667), guarded successes = 300/300 (1.0). The paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is: n11 = 299, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The preregistered exact McNemar two‑sided test returned p = 1.0. Absolute paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0033333333333332993. A paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI computed with B = 10000 resamples and seed = 1729 yields [0.00, 0.01]. Per‑stratum totals: low stratum 100/100 baseline & guarded; medium 100/100 baseline & guarded; high stratum baseline 99/100 vs guarded 100/100.

Repair diagnostic and transcript summary. The single discordant episode (n10 = 1) invoked the allowed automated repair. Validator traces attribute the initial flag to an omitted sequencing command required by the intent (a must_be_down_for_fields violation): the shared_initial candidate lacked an 'admin down' prior to a VLAN/MTU change. The constrained repair inserted the missing sequencing step; the deterministic validator subsequently reported valid == true for the repaired candidate. The low‑level repair provider trace, validator trace, and the shared_initial and repaired normalized configurations for this episode are archived in the run bundle; the manuscript provides a concise semantic summary here and the full provider trace is available in artifacts for forensic inspection.

Compact execution summary (artifact‑grounded). Table: key run totals and analysis results (values match archived CSVs and manifests).

- planned_episode_count: 600
- completed_episode_count: 600
- complete_pair_count: 300
- hosted_model_call_event_count: 301
- shared_initial_generation events: 300
- repair events invoked: 1
- baseline success rate: 299/300 = 0.9966667
- guarded success rate: 300/300 = 1.0
- paired counts (n11,n10,n01,n00): 299,1,0,0
- exact McNemar two‑sided p: 1.0
- bootstrap (B=10000, seed=1729) 95% CI for paired diff: [0.00,0.01]

Statistical interpretation. The near‑ceiling baseline produced only one discordant pair and therefore limited inferential sensitivity: the exact test p‑value of 1.0 reflects the paucity of discordant evidence under the shared_initial estimand. The bootstrap CI bounds the plausible absolute paired improvement at ≤1 percentage point in this experimental context. These inferential results apply strictly to the preregistered estimand and the tested synthetic suite; alternative estimands that permit resampling or larger repair budgets change both the analysis target and expected rescue opportunities.
sections.discussion:
Operational implications of the shared_initial estimand. Conditioning on a single LLM draw corresponds to operational policies that limit model calls per change request (e.g., cost, latency, or workflow constraints). Under such policies the guarded pipeline measures only deterministic validator and bounded repair rescue applied to the same candidate. By contrast, workflows that allow resampling, verifier‑guided generation, or interactive steering change the estimand and typically increase achievable success rates because they exploit generator variance. Organizations must therefore align evaluation estimands with operational constraints when selecting pipeline designs.

Ceiling effects and the unexecuted pilot. The preregistration targeted detection of a 10 percentage‑point absolute improvement with planned power ≈0.8, relying on pilot‑estimated discordance. Because the optional pilot (n = 60) intended to estimate discordance was not executed, the main run confronted a near‑ceiling baseline (299/300), producing minimal discordance (m = 1) and reduced power to detect small absolute differences. This underlines the value of small pilots for discordance calibration when the generator may perform near ceiling on chosen tasks.

Validator coverage and failure‑mode dependence. The observed single failure mode was a sequencing omission; other classes (reachability violations, forbidden ACL removal) were not observed at scale on this synthetic suite. The marginal value of a guarded pipeline therefore depends on the deployment distribution of failure modes and on validator expressiveness. A richer validator or a more adversarial/synthetic distribution emphasizing reachability or ACL invariants could increase observed rescue rates.

Repair budget and bounded automated edits. We limited automated repair to at most one constrained edit per pair to measure bounded deterministic rescue. That design measured only localized sequencing corrections; iterative repair, larger edit operators, or interactive verifier‑guided generation could increase rescue opportunities but test a different estimand. Our artifact bundle includes the single repair provider trace to permit detailed follow‑up analyses of repair efficacy and edit patterns.

Reproducibility and reproducible artifact grounding. All preregistration documents, task manifests, model configuration, raw responses, provider traces, validator traces, analysis CSVs, deterministic reconciliation, and analysis logs are archived under the study id. Analysis parameters (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729) and exact executor outputs are recorded. Deterministic reconciliation confirms episode accounting and provider call audits. These artifacts enable independent recomputation of the reported contingency counts and bootstrap CI with a deterministic executor. We emphasize that the shared_initial protocol and the archived shared_initial responses permit exact reproduction of the paired comparison without additional generator calls.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered, artifact‑archived paired comparison between a verifier‑assisted pipeline (deterministic validator + ≤1 automated repair) and accepting a single‑shot LLM candidate under the shared_initial estimand on 300 synthetic NetOps intents using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Baseline single‑shot generation produced 299/300 unflagged verifier passes and the guarded pipeline 300/300, yielding an absolute paired improvement of 0.00333 (exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.01]). Deterministic validator+repair rescued a single sequencing omission under the bounded repair budget. The near‑ceiling baseline limits inferential sensitivity to small absolute improvements under the shared_initial estimand. We release the preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts and recommend that future evaluations select estimands (e.g., allow resampling or expanded repair budgets) matched to operational policies when assessing the practical value of verifier‑assisted NetOps pipelines.

limitations: Synthetic benchmark: tasks and topologies were generated by the preregistered deterministic task generator; real‑world heterogeneity may expose different failure modes and increase verifier marginal utility.
Single model and validator: only gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 were evaluated; results may not generalize to other LLMs or richer/diverse validators.

Ceiling effect: baseline single‑shot performance was near 100% on this suite (299/300), producing limited discordance and reduced power to detect small absolute improvements relative to larger pre‑specified targets.
Pilot not executed: the preregistered pilot intended for discordance estimation and power calibration was not run; no post‑preregistration power recalculation was performed.

Estimand conditioning: the shared_initial protocol conditions the estimand on a single LLM candidate and therefore does not measure verifier benefit that would arise from allowing independent alternative LLM candidates per condition (resampling or iterative generation).
Repair budget: the guarded condition permitted at most one automated repair per pair; larger or iterative repair strategies may yield different outcomes.
